round6_research.bug_semantics: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File. The MCP server logs sensitive data to stderr via logger.debug: (a) src/api/ImageUploader.ts getUploadAuth() logs the full upload-credential/token response: `logger.debug('[ImageUploader] 上传凭证响应: ' + JSON.stringify(authRes).substring(0, 200))` - the upload auth response (Auth tokens / upload credentials) is dumped into logs; (b) src/api/HttpClient.ts logs every request URL: `logger.debug('[HttpClient] Request: ' + method + ' ' + fullUrl)` where fullUrl embeds signed query parameters (msToken, X-Bogus, a_bogus signature params, cookie-derived tokens); (c) src/server.ts logs full raw tool params: `logger.debug('Raw params received', { params: JSON.stringify(params, null, 2) })`. The logger's PII redaction only applies to context-object keys matching redactKeys; none of these sensitive values are passed as redacted context, and log lines go to stderr (and logs) unconditionally at DEBUG when DEBUG=true or at INFO for non-debug levels, so credentials leak into log files.

causal_research.bug_semantics: CWE-863 incorrect authorization: PUT /user is a write (including admin password change) but was gated by RequireScopes(profile:read). A stolen admin profile:read access token can change the password, then POST /login for a typ=session JWT that bypasses all RequireScopes checks.
evidence: First-party advisory CVE-2026-79673 / GHSA-6h3p-88p7-m8gp: Ech0 before 4.4.3 protects PUT /user with profile:read but allows writes including password changes; attacker then logs in for an unrestricted session token. CWE-863. Vendor write-up quotes internal/router/user.go PUT /user + RequireScopes(ScopeProfileRead), RequireScopes session bypass, and UpdateUser password assignment.

Design doc docs/dev/access-token-scope-design.md (landed 1ed191a5, 2026-03-23) listed both profile:read and profile:write. Implementation of the first scope vocabulary omitted ScopeProfileWrite and bound the write route to the read scope.

Smallest BIC is PR #195 pre-squash commit b47fa1c75d890cd080e3f6699bbfca8cd8d4b939 (feat(authz): enforce route-level scope checks). Patch first adds RequireScopes(ScopeProfileRead) on PUT /user (and other profile writes). Same commit correctly splits echo:read/write and file:read/write. Author/committer L1nSn0w <l1nsn0w@qq.com>; message trailer Made-with: Cursor.
BIC parent 1b280c252d1ef2ee69bf09f890d2da673b4b0a68 has PUT /user without RequireScopes. Confirmed via GitHub commit API file contents.

On default-branch history the same lines land in squash merge 3f8fb150158723aca31df2ae937a1aa7b31ac254 (feat(auth): enforce typed JWT and scoped access tokens #195), parent 45693330c7733364027e0aa07c102c4f01aab88a, which also lacks the RequireScopes binding. git blame -L 40,43 on v4.4.2 and git log -L 41,43 both point at 3f8fb150. Rejected as squash aggregate.

Version bounds: 3f8fb150 is first contained in tag v4.2.1 (v4.2.1~10). v4.2.0 PUT /user has no scope middleware. v4.2.1 and v4.4.2 still have ScopeProfileRead on PUT /user. v4.4.3 has ScopeProfileWrite. CVE 'before 4.4.3' matches; vendor 'affected <= 4.2.1' understates 4.2.2–4.4.2, which remain vulnerable.

Direct/closing fix 057e8b0b713d105eca7040ade810a057397613fa (2026-04-09) adds ScopeProfileWrite and switches PUT /user, OAuth bind, and passkey write routes from ScopeProfileRead to ScopeProfileWrite. Parent 2ccf950dcbb582b1c24147d0783a3397e9fe7354 still has ScopeProfileRead on PUT /user. Commit is v4.4.3~10 (ancestor of tag v4.4.3; not of v4.4.2). Later Huma/router refactors only preserve the write scope.

AI judged only on BIC object: human author L1nSn0w, not a bot account; explicit Made-with: Cursor trailer on b47fa1c and on the matching squash-message subsection. No Co-Authored-By. Ignore later AI trailers on unrelated refactors and on the fix (057e8b0b has none).
causal_research.reasoning: The vulnerability is the first scoped-token wiring of a password-changing write endpoint to a read-only scope, not the older UpdateUser password logic. That binding is new code in b47fa1c (squash-landed as 3f8fb150). The same Cursor commit implemented a read/write split for echo and file but left profile with only profile:read, contradicting the design vocabulary that already named profile:write. Made-with: Cursor on the BIC object is a generation marker, so the origin of the flawed authorization is AI-authored new code: AI_ROOT_CAUSE. Fix and BIC are both proven in public git.

causal_research.bug_semantics: The public, unauthenticated GET /ready readiness route attempted a database connection and SELECT 1 inside a broad exception handler, then serialized str(e) into the JSON response. A caller able to provoke a database/driver error could therefore receive internal database hostnames, IP addresses, ports, connection parameters, driver details, and potentially credentials embedded in the exception text.

causal_research.bug_semantics: PluginImportGuard.restore_hidden_modules() restored saved entries, cleared self.hidden_modules, and only then evaluated len(self.hidden_modules), so every restoration audit message reported zero regardless of the number restored. In setup, hide_dangerous_modules() deleted blocked modules from the process-global sys.modules before sys.meta_path.insert(0, import_guard) installed the blocking finder; a thread scheduled between those two operations could re-import a deleted blocked module and retain access to it, bypassing the intended sandbox in a multi-threaded process.
causal_research.flaw_origin: Commit e588aaa3a53ef291406b02745c20fdea8cea7f7c newly added PluginImportGuard and both causal mechanisms in openssl_encrypt/modules/plugin_system/plugin_sandbox.py: the clear-before-count restoration log and the non-atomic hide-then-install ordering. Its direct parent had no PluginImportGuard, hide_dangerous_modules(), or restore_hidden_modules().
causal_research.ai_marker: BIC commit object author and committer are Tobi <jahlives@gmx.ch> and its message contains the exact markers ‘🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)’ and ‘Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>’.
causal_research.evidence: The first-party advisory https://github.com/jahlives/openssl_encrypt/security/advisories/GHSA-43r4-3hf9-m84q identifies openssl_encrypt/modules/plugin_system/plugin_sandbox.py, the clear-before-log defect, the hide/import-hook race, affected range <1.4.0, and direct fix 85cdb6b. `git log -L '/^    def restore_hidden_modules/,/^    def find_module/':openssl_encrypt/modules/plugin_system/plugin_sandbox.py 85cdb6b...` has exactly the relevant origin e588aaa3a53ef291406b02745c20fdea8cea7f7c and change 85cdb6bedf3a0fbfb49e2f2e29cd66f1f36f3101; `git log --all -S'Restored {len(self.hidden_modules)}' -- .../plugin_sandbox.py` likewise shows e588 adding and 85c removing the vulnerable expression. The e588 patch adds the entire PluginImportGuard, stores/deletes blocked sys.modules entries, clears hidden_modules before logging its length, then calls import_guard.hide_dangerous_modules() before sys.meta_path.insert(). Direct parent-tree command `git grep -n -e 'class PluginImportGuard' -e 'restore_hidden_modules' -e 'hide_dangerous_modules' 5f8412ee11ac37e57190d6af4fe02f2cf7f2a5bd -- openssl_encrypt/modules/plugin_system/plugin_sandbox.py` returned no matches (exit 1), while the e588 diff is a 131-line addition containing the mechanism. `git cat-file commit e588...` proves the single parent, human author/committer, Claude Code generation line, and Claude Sonnet 4.5 co-author trailer in the BIC commit object. The 85c patch captures count before clear and adds a per-guard threading.Lock; its parent is 0c7418bab59e80a2b40913d8ad8523e6bbab196b. Version checks are unusually important here: `git tag --contains` for both e588 and 85c starts at v1.4.0; v1.3.6 source has no PluginImportGuard, while v1.4.0 contains `_modules_lock` and `logger.debug(f"Restored {count} hidden modules")`. Thus no tagged release in this clone contains the vulnerable interval, contradicting the advisory's literal '<1.4.0' package range; the flaw existed in pre-v1.4.0 branch history and the tagged v1.4.0 tree already contains the direct fix. Finally, inspection of 85c's tree shows hide_dangerous_modules() and sys.meta_path.insert() remain consecutive separate calls; the new private lock is acquired only inside hide/restore and is not acquired by other importing threads. Later cabda2c1dc4842ec737e3ad047fb0e3e4ee129af serializes threading-mode plugin execution and first appears in v1.4.1, but does not make arbitrary process threads honor the per-guard lock.
causal_research.reasoning: The smallest causal unit is e588, not a later refactor, merge, release, or fix: it is a normal one-parent atomic commit, its patch creates the guard and writes both exact flawed operations, -L/-S history traces the lines directly to it, and its immediate parent tree lacks the entire guard. The logging path is deterministic: clear makes the subsequently measured dictionary length zero. The race path follows directly from process-global mutation order: deletion occurs before finder installation, leaving a scheduler-visible interval in which ordinary import machinery has neither the cached module nor the blocking finder. The first-party direct remediation 85c fixes the logging value and declares the threading issue fixed; it precedes the v1.4.0 tag, as does the BIC, so the repository establishes a vulnerable development interval but not a vulnerable tagged version. The BIC commit object itself, without relying on PR text, branch names, or the AI-assisted fix, explicitly says it was generated with Claude Code and carries Claude Sonnet 4.5 as co-author. Because that AI-attributed BIC first authored the flawed mechanism, AI_ROOT_CAUSE is proven. The race portion should not be treated as conclusively closed by 85c: a lock used only by the same guard's hide/restore methods cannot synchronize unrelated Python imports, and the hide-to-hook ordering remains unchanged.
causal_research.remaining_gap: The logging subissue is patched by the advisory-named 85cdb6bedf3a0fbfb49e2f2e29cd66f1f36f3101, but the repository does not show a complete patch for the advisory's broader arbitrary-thread re-import window: 85c leaves deletion before hook installation and importing threads do not acquire `_modules_lock`. Also, tag ancestry disproves the published '<1.4.0' release range as written because pre-1.4.0 tags lack the guard and v1.4.0 already includes 85c. These are lifecycle/advisory defects, not gaps in BIC or AI attribution evidence.

Fixed by completing the denylist and removing the cwd discovery branch.

causal_research.bug_semantics: When a plugin lacked READ_FILES, PluginSandbox attempted to confine filesystem access by replacing only builtins.open with restricted_open. pathlib.Path.open/read_text/read_bytes/write_text/write_bytes and io.open retained independent file-opening paths, and pathlib/io were available to plugin code, so an untrusted plugin could read or modify paths outside the sandbox's allowed directories without passing _is_safe_path.
causal_research.flaw_origin: Commit 8a5ed7e62417441ed98b39481ac1a47510c1a9ef created the plugin sandbox and first implemented _restrict_file_operations as a single-name monkey patch: it assigned builtins.open = restricted_open but did not interpose io.open or pathlib.Path methods. The same commit advertised a zero-trust security sandbox, made this incomplete hook the READ_FILES enforcement boundary, and therefore originated the bypass rather than merely moving or refactoring existing vulnerable code.
causal_research.ai_marker: BIC commit object author and committer are Tobi <tobster@brain-force.ch>; its message contains the exact markers '🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)' and 'Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>'.
causal_research.evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/jahlives/openssl_encrypt/security/advisories/GHSA-mcjj-qw7m-j3cp identifies openssl_encrypt/modules/plugin_system/plugin_sandbox.py, demonstrates Path('/etc/passwd').read_text(), states the affected range as <1.4.0, and names d0be3e9 as the fix. In the validated clone, `git log d0be3e9^ -L 479,512:openssl_encrypt/modules/plugin_system/plugin_sandbox.py` follows the vulnerable function through formatting and policy changes to 8a5ed7e62417441ed98b39481ac1a47510c1a9ef, whose added lines 217-251 call _restrict_file_operations when READ_FILES is absent and replace only builtins.open. Independent `git log --all -S'builtins.open = restricted_open' -- openssl_encrypt/modules/plugin_system/plugin_sandbox.py` and `-S'def _restrict_file_operations'` each return only 8a5ed7e62417441ed98b39481ac1a47510c1a9ef. `git diff --name-status 649f737a9f04645508d079c0c772a8a2b4c7457a 8a5ed7e62417441ed98b39481ac1a47510c1a9ef -- openssl_encrypt/modules/plugin_system/plugin_sandbox.py` reports `A`, directly proving the entire vulnerable file and mechanism are absent from the immediate parent tree. `git cat-file -p 8a5ed7e62417441ed98b39481ac1a47510c1a9ef` proves the one-parent topology, human author/committer, Claude Code generation line, and Claude co-author trailer. `git show d0be3e989b1632eadb68e17d07294cbf9ac57c1f` shows the direct repair: save and replace io.open plus pathlib.Path.open/read_text/read_bytes/write_text/write_bytes/unlink/mkdir/rmdir, route each through the sandbox path check, and restore every original method afterward. Its immediate parent e0c999ea44429e8de00b4acb3ba570efdc733092 had added pathlib and io to shared blocked-module constants as precursor hardening, while d0be3e989b1632eadb68e17d07294cbf9ac57c1f is the advisory-named commit that directly interposes the bypassing APIs. `git tag --contains` places the BIC first in v1.3.0 (and all v1.3.x tags) but not v1.2.1, and places the fix first in v1.4.0 and later tags, matching the patched boundary.
causal_research.reasoning: The vulnerability lifecycle begins with the normal, one-parent feature commit 8a5ed7e62417441ed98b39481ac1a47510c1a9ef: its parent has no plugin_sandbox.py, and it introduces both the claimed READ_FILES boundary and the incomplete builtins.open-only enforcement. pathlib.Path uses pathlib/io entry points rather than the replaced builtins name, so the advisory's Path and io proof of concept bypasses the exact mechanism written by that commit. Later commits 642fb2bdec8af6f1d592c322dfa98647e145fcef and 35499f201ae2dc531d1194f6810c953d8b9af78b changed restoration and allowed-path policy while retaining that same single-hook design; ccb60e1a29ef67700128ca54eb25a95413d71ff1 only reformatted the relevant line. Thus blame is only a lead, while the -L history, two -S origin searches, and direct parent-tree addition establish 8a5ed7e62417441ed98b39481ac1a47510c1a9ef as the smallest real BIC, not a move, revert, backport, merge, or squash carrier. The first release containing it is v1.3.0; the advisory's direct atomic fix d0be3e989b1632eadb68e17d07294cbf9ac57c1f is first contained by v1.4.0, so the repository history refines the practical vulnerable interval to the v1.3.x releases within the advisory's broader <1.4.0 range. causal_research.bug_semantics: The unified FastAPI server enabled both JWT-protected modules by default while supplying public, hardcoded 39-character HS256 signing secrets for each module. Startup validation checked only that each secret was at least 32 characters and that the two values differed, so both defaults passed. Because TokenAuth.verify_token() trusted any correctly signed token with the module issuer and the route dependencies returned the attacker-controlled sub claim without requiring that client_id to exist, anyone knowing the source could forge a bearer token for an arbitrary client_id and reach authenticated keyserver upload/revocation and telemetry event APIs.
causal_research.flaw_origin: Single-parent commit 8170b3e0be064cdaddbc8ef51c17e21c42d2d3f4 created openssl_encrypt_server/config.py with the two known JWT defaults and the length-only validate_config(), and simultaneously created the HS256 TokenAuth and protected route dependencies that consumed those secrets. The immediate parent has no openssl_encrypt_server/config.py at all, and all-ref -S/log -L history identifies this commit as the first writer of the vulnerable defaults; no smaller pre-existing or reconstructable member commit contains them.
causal_research.ai_marker: BIC commit object author and committer are Tobi <jahlives@gmx.ch>, and its message contains the exact AI signals: "🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)" and "Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>".
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/jahlives/openssl_encrypt/security/advisories/GHSA-qc6h-gfjh-7qqg names openssl_encrypt_server/config.py, describes hardcoded defaults passing the >=32 check, states affected <1.4.0, and identifies resolution commit 6090a8e.

git log --all --full-history --reverse -S'keyserver-secret-change-me-min-32-chars' -- openssl_encrypt_server/config.py first returns 8170b3e0be064cdaddbc8ef51c17e21c42d2d3f4; git log -L 175,175:openssl_encrypt_server/config.py 6090a8e^ traces the keyserver default to that commit's creation of the file from /dev/null. The analogous telemetry default is blamed to the same commit.

At 8170b3e0be064cdaddbc8ef51c17e21c42d2d3f4, openssl_encrypt_server/config.py lines 75-83 set keyserver-secret-change-me-min-32-chars and telemetry-secret-change-me-min-32-chars. Each is 39 characters, so the same commit's validate_config() lines 143-159 accepts it under the only per-secret rule, len(secret) >= 32; server.py invokes validate_config(settings) during lifespan startup.

At the BIC, openssl_encrypt_server/core/auth/token.py signs and verifies HS256 JWTs using those configured secrets and validates only the module issuer cryptographically. modules/keyserver/routes.py and modules/telemetry/routes.py use payload.sub as authenticated client_id after best-effort update_last_seen(), without a required client lookup; protected sinks include POST /api/v1/keys, POST /api/v1/keys/{fingerprint}/revoke, and POST /api/v1/telemetry/events.

Direct parent-tree check `git cat-file -e 849da61d5e88aa901c6a8ec70859019a57156363:openssl_encrypt_server/config.py` fails because the path does not exist. The BIC is a one-parent commit, and all-ref content history exposes no earlier member commit containing either vulnerable default, so there is no reconstructable squash decomposition.

`git cat-file commit 8170b3e0be064cdaddbc8ef51c17e21c42d2d3f4` shows human author/committer Tobi plus the exact Claude Code generation line and Claude Sonnet 4.5 Co-Authored-By trailer. Only this BIC commit object was used for AI attribution.

6090a8e329230b5c4b941dcedee4cc4b78bb35a7 directly adds insecure-default marker checks to validate_config() and raises in the default non-debug mode before server startup, matching the first-party resolution. Later commit 8d0d91896ee19ea9c31951b39d72a364b594fd71 additionally removes the defaults, but it is subsequent hardening rather than the first direct fix.

Version cross-check: 8170b3e0be064cdaddbc8ef51c17e21c42d2d3f4 is not an ancestor of v1.3.6, while both it and 6090a8e329230b5c4b941dcedee4cc4b78bb35a7 are ancestors of v1.4.0 (peeled tag commit 768df5cd1910e349509f07a27eeac6951e0003bf). round6_research.bug_semantics: Sender-allowlist bypass (CWE-863) in the OpenClaw MSTeams extension (npm openclaw <=2026.3.28): in extensions/msteams/src/monitor-handler/message-handler.ts, when handling channel-message replies, the handler fetches the full thread history via the Graph API (fetchThreadReplies(graphToken, groupId, conversationId, activity.replyToId)) and injects ALL messages (parent + replies) into the model context via formatThreadContext(allMessages, activity.id) WITHOUT applying the sender allowlist. Direct and group messages go through allowlist enforcement (dmAllowFrom/effectiveGroupAllowFrom matchers), but reply-thread history bypasses it, so senders not on the allowlist can feed replies into the agent's context (medium severity, VI:L/SI:L). Fixed in v2026.3.31 by filtering thread messages through resolveMSTeamsAllowlistMatch when groupPolicy === 'allowlist'.

round6_research.bug_semantics: CVE-2026-54249 / GHSA-h7p7-w5gc-xj3w (PYSEC-2026-3692/3693, published ~2026-06, reporter via GitHub): UI adapters (Vercel AI and AG-UI) reconstruct file parts from client-submitted message history and forward them to model providers. FileUrl parts were validated against a scheme allowlist (allowed_file_url_schemes), but UploadedFile references - which point at a file by provider file ID or cloud-storage URI (s3://, gs://) - were forwarded with NO validation. The provider resolves an UploadedFile with server-side identity (IAM role / service account / provider API key), so a client that crafts message history containing an attacker-chosen UploadedFile can read arbitrary objects in the server's provider/cloud account (confused deputy / broken access control, CWE-284/863). Affected 1.65.0-1.105.0 and 2.0.0b1-b5; fixed in 1.106.0/2.0.0b6 by validating/dropping UploadedFile refs on client-submitted messages the same way file URLs are validated.

round8_research.bug_semantics: Server-side request forgery in the Webhooks API of backend-fix/complete_backend.js. POST /api/webhooks and PUT /api/webhooks/:id store caller-supplied fields (including url) by spreading req.body into the sampleWebhooks array without any URL validation. Commit 31dd902 then made the backend issue outbound HTTP requests to that stored URL with Node's global fetch: the /api/webhooks/:id/test endpoint posts a test payload to fetch(webhook.url), and /api/webhooks/notify plus the task create/complete lifecycle hooks post event messages to every active subscribed webhook's url. A client able to reach the API (no auth middleware; CORS allows no-origin requests and any origin when CORS_ORIGIN=*) can register/point a webhook at arbitrary destinations such as localhost admin ports, RFC1918 services or a cloud metadata endpoint, turning the documented backend into an SSRF relay, with the response status/error details echoed back in the test endpoint response.

causal_research.bug_semantics: When the optional webhook server is enabled, it listens on all interfaces and accepts POST requests containing an attacker-controlled exec string. Authentication is fail-open: WebhookServer.authenticate returns true whenever the configured token is empty, a state the configuration comments explicitly describe as 'empty = no auth'. The handler then dispatches req.Exec to a shell with -c/-Command. Thus an attacker who supplies a nonempty, reconstructable session_key (and a project when multiple projects are configured) can execute an arbitrary shell program as the cc-connect process without a credential. The shell interpretation of exec is an intentional feature; the security failure is exposing that full shell capability across a network endpoint while treating an omitted token as authorization.
causal_research.flaw_origin: The complete vulnerable mechanism originated in the single-parent feature commit 6ae088a658077a2f11a83ded6ac53c0dbddefd38: it created core/webhook.go, added the network listener and /hook handler, defined the JSON exec field, made an empty token authenticate successfully, passed exec to sh -c, wired the server into main, and documented an empty token as disabling authentication. This is the smallest repository-visible BIC, not the later shell-helper refactor.
causal_research.ai_marker: BIC commit object has human author and committer 'chenhg5 <chenhonggui@wps.cn>' and contains the exact message lines 'generated by llmgit' and 'Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>'. The latter is an explicit AI co-authorship trailer on the BIC itself.

Source review adds an important reachability qualification: handleHook requires a nonempty session_key, resolveEngine must succeed, and executeShell must reconstruct the named platform context. Consequently, the issue's displayed curl body, which omits session_key, would be rejected at the required-field check, but adding a valid/reconstructable session key reaches the confirmed unauthenticated shell path.

`git show 6ae088a658077a2f11a83ded6ac53c0dbddefd38 -- core/webhook.go config/config.go config.example.toml cmd/cc-connect/main.go` shows one cohesive +503-line webhook feature. In core/webhook.go it creates WebhookRequest.Exec, starts http.Server at fmt.Sprintf(":%d", ws.port), routes POST /hook through authenticate, returns true for ws.token == "", dispatches req.Exec, and runs exec.CommandContext(ctx, "sh", "-c", req.Exec). config/config.go and config.example.toml state that an empty token means no authentication, while main.go starts the listener whenever webhook.enabled is true.

Its immediate parent has no core/webhook.go or equivalent webhook-exec route, so absence is tree-proven. round6_research.bug_semantics: Replay of legitimately-signed policy snapshots (CWE-354 / CWE-347): ClearanceKit's on-disk policy store (/Library/Application Support/clearancekit/store.db, earlier user-policy.json) is signed with an EC-P256 key (System Keychain / Secure Enclave) and verified on load via PolicySigner, but the signed payload contains only the canonical row content with NO monotonic counter, version, or timestamp (freshness) binding. An attacker who can write store.db and the matching data_signatures row (feasible during the opfilter-update window when the Endpoint Security filter is offline, or via offline-boot / decrypted-backup scenarios) can substitute a previously captured legitimately-signed older snapshot; opfilter accepts it as fully valid on next boot because the ECDSA signatures still verify. Fixed in 5.0.10.
round6_research.evidence: Advisory identity: member map absent; alias-hash brute force (class_id == 'alias-'+sha256('\n'.join(sorted(members))+'\n').hexdigest()[:24], convention validated 20000/20000) over the repo_map pool (8 clearancekit advisories) yields the unique singleton CVE-2026-47133 (aliases: GHSA-9hx3-5wp9-2qqg, OSV GIT range introduced:0, fixed:afb9006638e4fd8bd1b134b26bb938b5b22d85b4, version 5.0.10). Introducer verified in clone: git show 4bb6687b0c -- Daemon/PolicySigner.swift = 199-line sign/verify with no counter; git show parent e43a3a28: no PolicySigner.swift, no signature verification of policy (only codesign-based XPC ConnectionValidator) -> introducer_parent_absent=true; 4bb6687b0c IS ancestor of the SQLite migration 1a49d9cb (first-child chain e43a3a28..1a49d9cb). round6_research.flaw_origin: Introduced 2026-03-15 by the first implementation of on-disk policy signing: commit 4bb6687b0c 'Sign on-disk policy with EC-P256 key in System Keychain / Secure Enclave' (Craig Bass <craig@madetech.com>, Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>) created Daemon/PolicySigner.swift (sign/verify primitives) and wired DaemonXPCServer.swift to sign policy on every save and verify on load, treating a valid ECDSA signature over the payload as sufficient authenticity with no freshness/epoch check. The design gap (no counter in signed payload) is inherent in this first writer; the SQLite data_signatures storage (1a49d9cb, 2026-03-15) and later PolicySigner rewrites (key-management changes 6cdf14cc/4b89e185/67146ddd/0216b95d/6e7965b8) preserved the counter-less scheme.

round6_research.bug_semantics: Proxy-only network fallback bypass on older Linux kernels (CWE-693, medium, CVSS 6.4 AV:L/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:L/A:N): on kernels without Landlock network rules (Landlock ABI < V4 / Linux < 6.7, e.g. 6.1), nono_py.sandboxed_exec() could run CapabilitySet.proxy_only(proxy) without supervising the seccomp-notify proxy-only fallback, so a sandboxed child could strip HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY or use raw sockets and open direct TCP connections (e.g. to cloud metadata 169.254.169.254) that proxy-only policy should have denied.
round6_research.evidence: Advisory GHSA-72w7-mf9g-733p (CVE id null): pip nono-py >=0.9.0,<0.10.1, first_patched 0.10.1, reviewed medium, CWE-693, reporter lukehinds, fix reference 3e67dfa11cbe9514f315fdd36473680c318816d7. Fix = 'Merge commit from fork' (2026-05-23, Luke Hinds, committer GitHub; parents 2897ee20 + 990389f8) 'feat(policy, python): enforce strict parsing and fail closed': src/policy.rs adds #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)] on RustPolicy/Group/AllowOps/DenyOps/NetworkOps/PolicyRouteConfig/PolicyEndpointRule, makes network block when network.block || network_requires_proxy(network) (allow_domain/credentials/custom_credentials/upstream_proxy/upstream_bypass/max_connections), + strict-parse and fail-closed tests; 10 files, 263 insertions. Fix is in v0.10.1 and v0.11.0+ (tag --contains first hit v0.10.1) and NOT in v0.10.0, matching first_patched 0.10.1. Introducer 16cd712 (author=committer Sambhav Kothari, single parent 753c9e5f, 2026-05-07) added proxy_only() to src/lib.rs (set_network_mode_mut(NetworkMode::ProxyOnly { port, bind_ports: Vec::new() })) + src/proxy.rs PortBinding + tests (215 lines); earliest tag containing it: v0.9.0 (2026-05-10), matching vulnerable range start >=0.9.0. Parent 753c9e5f src/lib.rs has 0 proxy_only and 0 ProxyOnly occurrences (verified via git show|grep -c). Commit body ends with 'Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>'. causal_research.bug_semantics: When the opt-in Management API is enabled with its token left empty, its authentication middleware treats the empty secret as successful authentication. The server listens on all interfaces at port 9820, and an unauthenticated remote POST to /api/v1/cron can copy attacker-controlled JSON exec text into a persisted CronJob. The cron scheduler identifies a nonempty Exec as a shell job and ultimately runs that text through the configured shell, so the attacker obtains command execution when the job fires; later code also added an immediate /api/v1/cron/{id}/exec trigger, but that was not necessary for the original scheduled-execution path.
causal_research.flaw_origin: The vulnerable trust-boundary crossing was created in one change: c2681402a7686294174a263e31245a52d4fea380 added the network-facing Management API, deliberately made authenticate return true for an empty token, registered the cron endpoints behind that fail-open middleware, and assigned untrusted req.Exec directly to CronJob.Exec. The shell-capable CronJob and its sh -c execution sink already existed in the parent; c2681402 is the smallest commit that made that sink reachable from an unauthenticated remote management request.

round6_research.bug_semantics: Information disclosure (CVE-2026-44653, CVSS 6.5, CWE-200/CWE-522): in LibreChat <= 0.8.3, GET /api/mcp/servers and GET /api/mcp/servers/:serverName returned the full MCP server config objects, including decrypted admin-managed secrets (apiKey.key and oauth.client_secret), to any authenticated user with only MCP USE or VIEW permission - including viewers of a shared MCP server who do not own it. The responses were raw registry/parsed configs with zero redaction, so non-owners could exfiltrate the underlying provider/API credentials. Fixed in 0.8.4 by redacting secrets from all server responses and validating configs.
round6_research.evidence: Advisory CVE-2026-44653 (identity brute-forced: alias = sha256 of the single id {CVE-2026-44653}; OSV full text: 'users with only VIEW access to an MCP server can retrieve the server's decrypted admin-managed secrets through GET /api/mcp/servers and GET /api/mcp/servers/:serverName... plaintext values for apiKey.key and oauth.client_secret... Version 0.8.4 contains a patch'; GitHub security advisory GHSA-6vqg-rgpm-qvf9; OSV GIT range introduced 0 -> fixed 0736ff26686e911c9785a237c63a799db1813f0b). Fix chain: 0736ff26 is the v0.8.4 release commit (PR #12339, Danny Avila <danny@librechat.ai>, 2026-03-20, 0 AI markers); the direct code fix is fa9e1b228a09fb02541068902635a97686eb32cc (PR #12217 'fix: MCP API Responses and OAuth Validation', Danny Avila, 2026-03-13, 0 AI markers), whose diff wraps getMCPServersList/getMCPServerById/updateMCPServerController/createMCPServerController responses in redactAllServerSecrets/redactServerSecrets from @librechat/api (new utils strip apiKey.key while retaining `source: 'admin'`, strip oauth.client_secret; jsdoc in controllers mcp.js: registry comment '(YAML + DB)'). Introducer forensics: git blame on the vulnerable return lines at fix parent f32907cd362c9d87b362661cd30a8f8a718fc864 attributes getMCPServersList's `return res.json(serverConfigs)` to ef1b7f015. AI-marker grep on ef1b7f015 %B = 4 matches: 'Chore: Work on AI Review and Copilot Comments', '- copilot comments addressed', plus 2 human Co-authored-by trailers (Atef Bellaaj slalom.bellaaj@external.daimlertruck.com, Danny Avila); same marker pattern on its sibling 1b0b27b30. #10787 commit bodies have only human Co-authored-by trailers (their 4 regex hits are all co-auth human trailers). Repo-wide: 141 commits mention 'copilot'; repo root carries CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md/CONTEXT.md AI-agent guidance; maintainer's squash messages are AI-assisted style.
round6_research.flaw_origin: First writer of the vulnerable response behavior: PR #10689 'refactor: Decouple MCP Config from Startup Config' (commits 1b0b27b30cc63a4c8b1ba65cc2146c7857008439 for the packages/api registry pieces and ef1b7f0157091f56ad1e6c4fd8133e4c191eed12 for api/server, both Atef Bellaaj <atef.bellaaj@slalom.com>, 2025-11-26) introduced the GET /api/mcp/servers list endpoint; getMCPServersList at introduction returns `res.json(serverConfigs)` where serverConfigs = mcpServersRegistry.getAllServerConfigs(userId) '(YAML + DB)' - i.e. admin-managed YAML configs AND user DB configs, secrets included, with only requireJwtAuth and no redaction. Parent 98b188f26c5b61c60bc3e1f79f18dd0f00341c32 has no getMCPServersList and no '/servers' route in api/server/routes/mcp.js (grep count 0 for both route and controller) -> vulnerable behavior absent -> atomic introducer.
